supporting_observations.claim: The session to FILE-RB-01 came from WS-CPRICE-01 (10.60.10.22), not the designated administrative workstation WS-DSHARMA-01. WS-CPRICE-01 records dev.sharma signing in interactively, launching mstsc.exe for FILE-RB-01, and FILE-RB-01 accepting a type-10 remote interactive logon for dev.sharma from that workstation. This conflicts with the stated rule that server administration is only performed from WS-DSHARMA-01.

During the same WS-CPRICE-01 interactive session, a PowerShell process on that workstation made an explicit-credentials event targeting svc-rbbackup on FILE-RB-01. The supplied record does not establish what command or action followed.
The RDP session ended at approximately 14:03:38 UTC, according to the type-10 logoff record for dev.sharma on FILE-RB-01.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records establish the RDP connection and logon, but do not show the commands or actions performed within that remote session.

The explicit-credentials event identifies PowerShell and the target account and server, but supplies no command line or corresponding evidence establishing whether authentication or an operation succeeded.
The available records do not establish who was physically or otherwise controlling WS-CPRICE-01 at the time.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish that dev.sharma's credentials were stolen or that someone other than dev.sharma used them.
The evidence does not establish malicious intent, data access or exfiltration, malware execution, or changes made on FILE-RB-01.
The supplied evidence does not establish whether the open VetChart hang ticket authorized any of this server access.
additional_evidence_needed: Review the ticket and change records for authorization covering the RDP session and any activity from WS-CPRICE-01.
Collect FILE-RB-01 session process, command-line, file-access, and account-change telemetry for the RDP logon ID 0x11c5e164.
Investigate the WS-CPRICE-01 PowerShell event, including its full command line, process ancestry, script or module logs, and any authentication or access records for svc-rbbackup.
Confirm with dev.sharma whether they initiated the session and determine why administration occurred from WS-CPRICE-01 rather than WS-DSHARMA-01.
